entries.title: The Shepherd Who Looks After Me
entries.text:
Yahweh is the shepherd who looks after me.
I will never lack anything.
entries.reflection:
A shepherd stays close to the sheep. He watches the path, the weather, and the places where grass and water can be found. The sheep do not have to figure all of that out alone. Psalm 23 begins with that picture. Yahweh is the shepherd who looks after me.

The next line says, "I will never lack anything." A good shepherd sees to what the sheep need: food, a path, and a watchful eye. Wants and needs are not always the same thing. Some days still feel short on time, money, health, or peace. Those hard days are real. This verse sets them inside a larger care. I am looked after. My life is shared with a shepherd who walks beside me.

So today I can ask for what I need. I can also notice what has already been given. The shepherd is already on this road with me. I can walk it as someone who is known and kept.
entries.prayer: Yahweh, my shepherd, look after me today. You see what I need. Lead me, feed me, and keep me close to you. Give me a quiet heart that can rest in your care, and thank you for walking this road with me. Amen.

entries.title: A Hiding Place and Strength
entries.text:
God is our hiding place and our strength,
always ready to help in trouble.
entries.reflection:
Trouble shows up in this verse as a normal part of the road. God meets us there. He is our hiding place and our strength, always ready to help.

A hiding place is where a person can catch their breath and tell the truth about being afraid. Strength is what helps them take the next step. God is both at once. Always ready means his help meets us at the start of the trouble, while the fear is still fresh. We can turn to him while our hands are still shaking.

Hiding, in this psalm, is how we find our feet again. We rest long enough to stand, then we go back to the people we love and the work in front of us. When a hard day comes, we can start with a simple prayer: be my shelter, and be my strength. He is already ready to help.
entries.prayer: God, you are my hiding place and my strength. I bring you the trouble I am carrying. Shelter me, and give me strength for the next true thing in front of me. Thank you that you are always ready to help. Amen.

entries.title: Trust Completely
entries.text:
Trust Yahweh completely.
Do not lean on what you understand yourself.
entries.reflection:
Trust Yahweh completely. The proverb then tells us where to put our weight. Our own understanding is too small to carry all of it.

Proverbs also spends line after line teaching people to pay attention, to learn, and to choose with care. A mind that thinks is a gift. Trust and careful thought belong together. The warning is about weight. When we lean, we rest our full weight on something. If the only thing holding us up is our own view of a situation, that view will sometimes be too small. We cannot see the end of a choice from the middle of it. We cannot see what a year will ask of us.

To trust Yahweh is to include him in the choice and to let his wisdom carry what ours cannot. We can pray before we decide. We can ask for a clear mind and a humble one. Then we can act, with open hands, even while some questions are still unanswered.
entries.prayer: Yahweh, I trust you with this whole day. Give me a clear mind and a humble one. Guide the choice in front of me, and teach me to include you in it. I place what I cannot see into your hands. Amen.

entries.title: Brave While You Wait
entries.text:
Wait for Yahweh.
Be strong and brave in your heart.
Yes, wait for Yahweh.
entries.reflection:
Wait for Yahweh. The psalm says it twice, with a charge in the middle: be strong and brave in your heart. Waiting and bravery are placed side by side. This wait is a steady heart turned toward God while an answer is still on the way.

Most of us would rather hold the answer than hold the wait. We fill the quiet with worry, or we push on a door because the right one has not opened. The psalm calls the heart back. The strength it names sits in the heart, the place where fear speaks the loudest. Bravery there can look quiet from the outside. It can look like honest prayer, a kept promise, or a soft heart on a day when the way through is still hidden.

Yes, wait for Yahweh. He is worth waiting for. The thing we placed in his hands is still in his hands.
entries.prayer: Yahweh, I am waiting for you. Make my heart strong and brave while I wait. Keep me steady, honest, and hopeful. I place this hope in your hands again. Help me wait for you. Amen.

entries.title: The God Who Does Not Get Tired
entries.text:
Do you not know? Have you not heard?
Yahweh is the everlasting God,
the Creator of the ends of the earth.
He does not get tired or worn out.
No one can measure his understanding.
entries.reflection:
Isaiah asks a question that works as a reminder: Do you not know? Have you not heard? It is easy to forget the answer on a day when we are tired. Yahweh is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth. He does not get tired or worn out. No one can measure his understanding.

Set that beside a long evening, when the mind is full and the body is done. We run out of strength. He does not. The verse meets us in that weariness and tells us who is still strong.

Everlasting means he has no beginning and no end. Creator of the ends of the earth means the far places we will never see are his, and so is the room where we are sitting. His understanding is wider than anything we can measure. That is a gift when our own understanding has reached its edge. We can bring him a problem we cannot sort out. We can also bring him nothing but our tiredness. He is still listening, and he is not worn out.
entries.prayer: Everlasting God, you made the ends of the earth, and you never grow tired. I bring you my weariness and the questions I cannot measure. Stay with me, and give me the strength I need for today. Amen.

entries.title: Faithful and Present
entries.text: Nobody will withstand you as long as you live. I stood by Moses, and I will stand by you in the same way. You will find me faithful and present; I will not leave you.
entries.reflection:
These words were spoken to Joshua, as he took up the work Moses had carried. God says he stood by Moses, and he will stand by Joshua in the same way. "You will find me faithful and present; I will not leave you."

Joshua had a heavy task in front of him. God speaks to that weight with a promise about his own character. He is faithful. He is present. He stays with the person he sends, and he does not walk off once the work begins.

Our days are different from Joshua's days, and our work is our own. What we can hold from this verse is the way God stays. When a task feels too big, we can ask for that same company. We can tell him we need him to be faithful and present here. Then we can take the next small step with God beside us.
entries.prayer: Yahweh, you are faithful and present. You stood with your servants, and you stay with them. Be with me in what is too big for me. Help me take the next step with you beside me. Amen.

entries.title: Close to the Brokenhearted
entries.text:
Yahweh is close to people with broken hearts.
He rescues those whose spirits are crushed.
entries.reflection:
Some pain makes a person feel far from other people, and far from God as well. Psalm 34 says Yahweh is close to people with broken hearts. He rescues those whose spirits are crushed.

Close is a near word. God comes close to the person who is hurting. In this verse a broken heart is a place where he draws near. Crushed is an honest word too. The psalm lets the hurt stay as large as it is. God comes anyway.

Rescue is his real help. Some losses are still losses this afternoon, and the ache may still be there at night. His rescue means we are met inside that hurt by someone who can help. We can tell him the true size of it. We can sit with this verse when our spirit is crushed: he is close, and he rescues. We are held by a God who comes near.
entries.prayer: Yahweh, you are close to people with broken hearts. Come near to me. You know the true size of this hurt. Rescue me, and stay close so I know you are here. Amen.
